elements.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Rendered Section 14.3 retains "This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of California, USA"; no New York choice of law was proposed. The drafter deliberately targeted the fallback.

elements.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
elements.evidence: The rendered forum is "the state and federal courts located in San Francisco County, California," not New York County; no temporary-injunctive-relief carve-out is included (the drafter states this was intentionally omitted as preferred-only).

elements.element: The governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: Retained operative text: "This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of California, USA, excluding conflict of laws provisions..." California is within the accepted fallback set; deterministic check "governing law within the accepted set" passes.

elements.element: The dispute forum is the corresponding Delaware or California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: Rendered: "Any disputes arising out of this Agreement shall be resolved exclusively in the state and federal courts located in San Francisco County, California, and each party consents to the exclusive jurisdiction of such courts." The mandatory AAA arbitration mechanic and single-arbitrator appointment are deleted, so California courts now hear the merits and the forum matches the California governing law.

reasons: The fallback checklist is complete: California law is retained (already met) and the arbitration forum is replaced with exclusive jurisdiction of the California state and federal courts in San Francisco County, which is the forum corresponding to the retained governing law.
The preferred level is not reached because neither New York law nor New York County courts are proposed; that is acknowledged and acceptable because the redline targets the fallback.

Minimality holds. Only the jurisdiction/forum words were changed: the conflict-of-laws exclusion, the CISG exclusion and the balance of Section 14.3 survive verbatim. The deleted sentences (AAA rules reference, single-arbitrator appointment, judgment-on-award, AAA fee allocation) are all arbitration-specific machinery that could not survive removal of arbitration without contradiction, so their deletion is necessary rather than cosmetic. No extras (no injunctive-relief carve-out, no fee-shifting substitute, no procedure or survival tail) were added.

Intent is preserved. The heading is conformed to "Choice of Law; Venue," and the Section 12.2 cross-reference is changed from "referred to arbitration in the manner provided in Section 14.3" to "resolved in the manner provided in Section 14.3," so the escalation mechanic (ten business days of officer negotiation, then referral) still functions and no dangling reference to arbitration remains. The termination triggers, cure period and notice mechanics in that paragraph are untouched.

Residual point for the drafter to confirm, not a defect on the record shown: the defined term "RULES" was created in the deleted arbitration sentence. It is used only within the deleted text here, but confirm no other section of the Agreement references "Rules," which would otherwise leave an undefined term.

Classification as a deviation is correct: the seat was domestic (San Francisco), so the original clause was not walk-away, but mandatory binding arbitration defeats the fallback forum element on a material term and warranted a redline.
